notes.title: Content Update 1.15
notes.content:
Hey! 😎
It's time for a proper quality of life content update. This one's coming to you with the new unlockable game mode "Waves".

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44211860/a50b89af0e81e5fca2646b0d4417879731ce2aaa.gif

The new Waves mode features 3 games: Score attack, Survival and Custom. The first two game types are connected to a global leaderboard; get the highest kill score or survive for the longest time! In "Custom" games you can play around with your own time and waves limit without competition. Unlock this mode by completing the game and get the Waves mode achievement.

There's also some graphical updates, which improves the post-processing effects and the resolution scaling. 

And last but not least: a new weapon - straight from Lang's private collection! This one's got some huge kickback.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44211860/3a66f17ee82b740e68ca3e4d0177036c7cb2c845.gif

Fixes and additions:

Added unlockable game mode "Waves" with leaderboards.
Added Dithering filter option to settings panel with default setting OFF.
Added new weapon: "Wessersmith" revolver (from Lang's "private collection").
Adjusted resolution scaling.
Updated post-processing effects.
Updated objectives descriptions.
Updated dialogue UI to better distinguish between keyboard and controller inputs.
Some minor bug fixes and adjustments.

That's it for now!
[previewyoutube=gj5HzO0GmtE;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: What's next?
notes.content:
Hello!
It's been some time since the last update. I've been working on adding some more unlockable content that will increase the quality of life of the game.

Here's a sneak peak at the Waves mode, which features 3 different games:

Score attack: Get the highest score over 10 minutes.
Survival: Survive for the longest time.
Custom: Play at your own custom settings. This game is not counted towards the leaderboards.

[previewyoutube=gj5HzO0GmtE;full][/previewyoutube]
The waves of enemies will get progressively more difficult. Hopefully you'll gain enough score or survive for as long as possible to grab a spot on the global leaderboard!

Look for this mode in the upcoming update and unlock it by completing the game.

Until next time!

Let me start with the good news: The latest version of the game is uploaded and ready to be released on Steam. 

The bad news: I've run into a pretty serious game engine bug (yes, Unity), which has messed up the main scene file. Luckily I had already built and uploaded the latest version before this happened, so the release can go ahead as scheduled. Unfortunately, this hiccup will probably cause significant delays to possible future updates.

I wanted to be as upfront about this as possible so you know what's going on and to set future expectations accordingly regarding game updates.

For now, I will take a step back to take a breather and review the situation. Hopefully this should be fixed as soon as possible. Thank you for your patience and understanding!

Until next time!

notes.title: A not-so-technical write-up of Zero Below The Sun
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44211860/7b062e2be9be1387ecfd4c5521767ff9e729dab7.png
Intro
Zero Below The Sun is a retro style action survival horror game, set in Antarctica. You play as Axel Bowers, a security officer at a top-secret underground facility somewhere in Antarctica. The game starts off with the facility going into lockdown and it's your task to investigate what is going on. The player must navigate the multi-level facility to collect clues, weapons and find survivors - sometimes friendly and sometimes not. It soon becomes clear that the purpose of the facility is much more sinister than you could've imagined, as you discover unthinkable horrors prowling the gloomy hallways.

Background
Zero Below The Sun is a game I've wanted to make for many years. I always knew that I wanted to make a survival horror type game of some sorts, but what kind? There are so many - the indie survival horror scene has steadily been growing over the past years - and I didn't just want to make just "another Resident Evil clone". The game has evolved during the development from an idea that started out like a shorter arcade type survival horror experience, to a much more traditional action-adventure oriented one. To describe the game with one word, I would say "quirky".

Visuals
The visual style I was aiming for is a bit stylized, especially for the characters which are to some degree almost cartoonish in appearance. However, the environments got a somewhat more realistic style. The game features a retro low-polygon aesthetic, with a heavily restricted polygon count and texture resolution to give that overall pixelated look. At first I was going for a flat polygon look, but later decided to scrap it in favor for smooth polygons as it was a better fit for the style I was going for.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44211860/aa7aa8bd109cdaf74a15b8f6976107d74620fcd6.png
Below is the first ever screenshot taken from the prototyping phase, back in 2020.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44211860/fb64513361c4f8d5b758a98bb44cd7ad448b1ec7.png

Level Design
When looking at the environments and its textures, I've gone for a pretty drab and muted color palette. In contrast, the character and NPC textures are generally pretty colorful so that they "pop out" from the environments. This gives the game a rather unique look; playful yet ominous. The general level design is made up of hallways and connecting rooms, some of which are open areas. The whole facility consists of multiple floors that are connected via elevators. There's also an outdoor area, as I also wanted to incorporate a bit of snow seeing as the game is set in Antarctica.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44211860/1b0ced396d157b44f9cf883ac2f84b46c078def2.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44211860/2ac7a55766bb778036c3f75e11d330bf4fac9193.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44211860/db87695e307003dfc805a078f1c3bba4d41abe0a.gif

Character Design
As for the character designs, I started by making the player model to establish a overall in-game style for the rest of the characters. The "paddle" hands that are quite prominent on the player character were an accidental design during prototyping and was originally intended to be changed by adding a thumb in the final design. However, seeing people's positive feedback early on in the development made me decide to keep it as is. For the protagonist, Axel Bower, I wanted to tick all the boxes of survival horror clichés to create an over-the-top action hero. He got the spiky hair, the leather jacket, the jeans and the shades, which he wears at all time in-doors and has become rather iconic over time.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44211860/5f60a3544f47b057fa5256fbf94347c07740c361.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44211860/2f6d257b61fc7947939cbac8994a8d18507a8057.gif
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44211860/a0184e6b0d5901372e0d3551bfca255217e8e907.png

Game Design
On the surface, Zero Below The Sun may look like just another indie survival horror game. As previously stated, I didn't want to make "just another survival horror game" or "Resident Evil clone". So, I opted not to go for the classical fixed-camera style that's popular among the genre and instead went with a free camera in a fully 3D rendered environment. This way I could create a much more action-oriented survival horror game with more intense combat scenarios.

The writing of the game is probably were the game sets itself apart the most. While I've stayed true to many of the traditional survival horror tropes, I've also tried to make the game not take itself too seriously. By this I mean that the in-game dialogues and interactions between the characters are often on the lighter side and sometimes also incorporates a bit of humor. This, in combination with a bit of janky keyframed animations, presents the game with a bit more unique personality.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44211860/29a291572fad82acda0040c8e934deadcb82f3e8.gif

To summarize, Zero Below The Sun is a traditional survival horror in its core, but takes a more action-oriented approach and blends easily digested story telling with a bit of tongue-in-cheek character dialogues. If you are looking for a retro styled survival horror that's a bit quirky, I think you will enjoy the game. The full game will be available 2 Aug 2024.

That's it for now. Until next time!

notes.title: General Q and A
notes.content:
Hey!
Here's a quick Q n' A of some questions that has popped up lately.

What is "Zero Below The Sun"?

Zero Below The Sun is a survival horror game, inspired by the classic survival horrors of the 90's with a retro aesthetic in full 3D and over-the-shoulder camera view. This means that the game, to an extent, features some 3rd person shooter action. You can also expect some classic puzzle solving, finding clues to uncover more pieces of the story and interacting with some NPCs; friendly and unfriendly. Your main goal is to find out what has happened at the base and to make it out alive.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44211860/c08384c21dd8a75c571f208ad7642b7d42a0ad59.gif

Is this game based on John Carpenter's movie "The Thing"?

Short answer: No. 
There are some small inspirations drawn from this movie, but the game is in no way based on this movie nor does it have any connections or any sort of relation to it.

How long is the demo?

Approx. 20-30 minutes.

How long is the full game?

Expect at least 3 hours for a blind play-through.

Why is the game running in 30 fps?

The game runs at 30 fps (frames per second) by default for retro aesthetic reasons, but you can change this in the in-game settings.

How does the weapons work?

There are several weapons that you will find in the game and each one has different pros and cons. The handgun you will likely find more ammunition for, so it's a good all-rounder. Then there's a SMG which uses burst fire; slightly more powerful than the handgun, but the ammunition is more rare. The Assault rifle is the only weapon which fires full-auto, at a similar damage level as the SMG. The latter also has an optional scope Mod Disk.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44211860/d44fdd2755638c0e62cb7020b93933042040050b.gif

Why can I only equip one Mod Disk at a time?

The Mod Disk are a power bonus, which enhances the weapons in certain ways. For the handgun you can find a laser sight mod and a damage amplifier, for instance. As this is a survival horror game, I don't want to make the weapons over-powered - only give them a slight boost, which can be helpful in certain situations.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44211860/db681e4973209c50b2e327f7726864b5f47ccc73.png

Are there any achievements?

Yes. At the time of writing there are 18 Steam achievements in the full version of the game. They vary from finding different weapons to performing headshots or by simply not killing anything at all (except for bosses). There will also be hidden unlockables.

That's it for now. Until next time!
